Without the `!`, vars would be (string|undefined)[] and quoteIdentifierIfNecessary(vars[0]) would not type-check, so the assertion is what let the crash-prone call compile; but the real undefined comes from an empty array (no noUncheckedIndexedAccess), so the causal framing is loose and the line predates the diff.

cleanTableName strips only ['"()] and splits at the first space, so the now-default `FROM \`gdp per capita\`` yields target "`gdp", Graph.link throws for a nonexistent node, and createDAGFromQueriesSafe rejects the SQL expression; the PR generates such queries by default (alerting refIds are renamable) without fixing the DAG parser.

The third argument is asserted with expect.anything(), which matches [] so a failed refId lookup goes unnoticed — the same gap thread 7 raises about the source-query lookup in fetchSQLFields being untested.

mysql is a decoupled plugin workspace (own package.json/webpack config, listed under grafana/decoupled-plugins-overrides) and no other core code imports from it; core depending on a plugin internal is a real but small dependency-direction concern, not blocked by lint.

Monaco's mysql grammar emits the backtick as its own identifier.quote token, getTableToken returns it, fetchSQLFields re-quotes it and its refId filter matches nothing so column completion returns []; this is the production read-back defect thread 7 describes (quoted query.table vs raw refId lookup).
True label change for previously-saved (broken) unquoted initial queries, but self-declared not a defect — a cleared note.
With refIds empty vars[0] is undefined and isValidIdentifier calls identifier.toUpperCase() → TypeError during render, where it previously rendered 'FROM undefined'; exactly thread 0.

The editor uses Monaco's mysql language configuration whose autoClosingPairs are {}, [], (), ", ' — no backtick pair — so a typed backtick is not auto-closed and the doubled-backtick scenario does not arise.
